title: Redwood PLG quickstart discovery - Montage Labs
summary: Initial PLG quickstart discovery focused on trying Redwood hosted API vs Dedicated. Customer wants fast time-to-first-token, free credits for evaluation, and clarity on security (SOC2/KMS) and cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps include sending pricing, security docs, and scheduling a technical deep dive for infra team.
next_steps: Jamie Park: Send Dedicated and Hosted pricing matrix
Sofia Martinez: Share SOC2 and security deck + SSO/KMS integration notes
Jamie Park: Provision free credits and invite Montage to Redwood account
Schedule SE-led technical deep dive with Montage infra (target next week)
Customer to try quickstart and report time-to-first-token

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Montage CTO), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Marco Alvarez (VP Product)

[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood, and with me is Sofia, our solutions engineer. Quick agenda: understand your goals, walk through quickstart options, free credits, and figure out next steps.
[00:18] Ethan: Thanks Jamie, yeah, time is tight so we wanna get to time-to-first-token—how fast can our engineers go from sign-up to calling the API. We're evaluating hosted first, maybe Dedicated later.
[00:32] Sofia: Totally, our PLG quickstart is designed for that—sign up, get free credits, SDKs, and a one-file example. Typical teams hit first token in under 15 minutes if they have their API key.
[00:47] Priya: Nice, what's involved on the infra side? We have some compliance constraints—need SOC2, SSO, and option for private deployment later.
[00:58] Jamie: Yeah, that's common. Hosted is easiest for quick evals—usage-based pricing, free credits. Dedicated is reserved capacity for predictable throughput and data isolation; Private is VPC/on-prem for strict regs. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS notes.
[01:15] Marco: For us latency matters for interactive features—sub-200ms is ideal but cost is also a factor. How do you balance that?
[01:25] Sofia: Good question. There's tradeoffs—smaller models + quantization cut cost but increase latency sometimes; Dedicated with pinned GPUs gives consistent latency. Also we do autoscaling and smart routing so you can route by latency SLOs.
[01:38] Ethan: Can we run benchmarks? Like the same prompt across Hosted and Dedicated to see delta?
[01:44] Sofia: Yes, we can run a benchmark with your prompts. We'll set up a canary on Dedicated and compare throughput and p99 latency. I can run a short eval if you give a prompt set.
[01:55] Priya: About time-to-first-token, how long is the signup flow and any infra approval? We have to get legal sign-off for data retention.
[02:04] Jamie: Self-serve signup is immediate. Free credits are provisioned automatically or we can pre-provision for your team. Legal/compliance for Production Dedicated or Private will take longer—we can provide docs for procurement.
[02:17] Marco: On data retention—do you store customer data? How does logging/audit work?
[02:22] Sofia: Hosts usually retain call metadata for billing and debugging, you can opt into retention policies; Dedicated gives you stronger isolation and we integrate with KMS for encryption at rest. We'll send the security deck.
[02:34] Ethan: Any gotchas around KV cache or streaming that we should know about? Our use case is chat with long context.
[02:42] Sofia: For long context we manage KV cache and support quantization-friendly execution. Continuous batching helps cost but may add a bit to latency; you can tune batching in Redwood Console. There might be some transcription of internal terms—Redwood's runtime has attention optimizations, etc.
[03:00] Marco: Pricing model? We want to compare per-token hosted cost vs reserved monthly for Dedicated.
[03:06] Jamie: Hosted is per-token plus embed units; Dedicated is flat reserved capacity with lower marginal unit cost and SLAs. We'll send a side-by-side pricing matrix.
[03:18] Priya: Security integrations—SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs—are those available for hosted?
[03:26] Sofia: SSO and RBAC are available for enterprise hosted accounts; audit logs and longer retention are add-ons. Private gives full control over network and KMS/HSM.
[03:37] Ethan: For quickstart, do you have SDKs and examples for our stack? We're a Node + FastAPI backend.
[03:44] Jamie: Yes, official SDKs for Node and Python. We also have quickstart templates for common frameworks—like a sample FastAPI endpoint. The goal is less than 15 minutes to first token in most cases.
[03:57] Marco: Ok, if we sign up today, can we demo something to internal stakeholders within a day?
[04:02] Jamie: Absolutely—we'll provision credits today and send a one-click quickstart repo.
[04:08] Sofia: If you want, we can also spin up a small Dedicated trial for benchmarks, but that requires a short procurement step.
[04:16] Ethan: How do fallbacks work if Dedicated capacity hits a limit?
[04:21] Sofia: We have smart routing and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants or Hosted capacity so apps don't break—graceful degradation.
[04:30] Marco: Any notes on model catalog? We use an LLM for summarization and embeddings as well.
[04:36] Jamie: Redwood API supports text gen, chat, embeddings, reranking. Model catalog lists curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. We also have recommendations for quantization and batching.
[04:48] Priya: For embeddings, are those billed differently?
[04:51] Jamie: Yes, embeddings have separate unit pricing; we'll include that in the pricing matrix.
[04:56] Ethan: On the security docs—do you publish SOC2 reports or is that on request?
[05:01] Sofia: We can share SOC2 Type II and some compliance artifacts under an NDA or via a secure portal. We'll attach the deck and KMS integration notes.
[05:12] Marco: Ok, what's the typical timeline if we move from evaluation to Dedicated?
[05:17] Jamie: From POC to Dedicated—if you commit to reserved capacity it's usually a few weeks for provisioning and tests; Private deployments take longer depending on networking.
[05:25] Priya: Can you walk us through a sample quickstart flow? Maybe Sofia can?
[05:30] Sofia: Sure—sign up, verify email, create API key, clone quickstart repo, set API key env var, run sample request. If you want, we can script that into a short demo.
[05:42] Ethan: Sounds straightforward. For benchmarking, we'll share 10-15 representative prompts and a couple of sample documents.
[05:49] Sofia: Great; send them to me, I'll run hosted and small dedicated tests, share p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:58] Marco: Any limitations on model size or custom models? We may want to bring our fine-tuned weights later.
[06:05] Sofia: Right now Redwood supports onboarding of open models and some customer-managed models for Dedicated/Private. For private model deployment we'd need more details but it's supported.
[06:17] Jamie: Quick recap—action items: we'll send pricing and security docs, provision free credits, and schedule a technical deep dive. Montage will share prompts and infra contacts.
[06:29] Ethan: Perfect. One more quick question: does Redwood offer pre-built evals or regression alerts?
[06:35] Sofia: Yes, Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals—good for production rollouts.
[06:44] Marco: Great. If all looks good from the POC we'll discuss Dedicated sizing and reserved commit.
[06:50] Jamie: Thanks everyone—I'll follow up with the materials. Next steps in notes.

End of transcript.
